brief.headline: The entire LME base-metals board settled lower on 27-August as the dollar firmed, and aluminium gave back most of the previous session's Hormuz-driven jump - but the aluminium curve quietly flattened to a $3.50 contango while the price fell, and copper's and zinc's backwardations widened to the widest of the window, so across the board the front end outperformed the back.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the LME aluminium cash official settled at $3,212.50 on 27-August, down $15.00 (-0.46%), and three-month at $3,216.00, down $23.00 (-0.71%). Every metal on the board fell on the three-month - nickel -1.23%, zinc -1.09%, aluminium -0.71%, copper -0.70%, lead -0.21% - and lead's cash was the only settlement on the board to rise, up $6.00. Exchange aluminium stock did not move for a third consecutive session: 246,825 tonnes, published change exactly zero.

WHY IT MOVED: the EUR/USD LME fixing fell to 1.16410 from 1.16690, a firmer dollar, which reprices an entire dollar-denominated board lower without any metal-specific news being required. Alongside that, part of the Hormuz risk premium came back out: Iran and Oman have publicly outlined a phased framework for a temporary shipping corridor with a 30- to 60-day negotiating window toward a permanent route and a joint mine-clearing initiative, and Oman's foreign minister said he was hopeful it would soon be formalised. The strait itself nevertheless remains effectively closed to commercial shipping, so this is a negotiation headline, not a reopening.

THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THAT IS THE DETAIL WORTH KEEPING: aluminium's contango narrowed to $3.50 from $11.50 - a nearly flat curve and the flattest of the fifteen-session window - because cash fell $15.00 while three-month fell $23.00. Copper did the same far more violently, cash off only $35.00 against a $100.00 fall in three-month, widening its backwardation to $254.00 with stock down another 1,900 tonnes to 235,575. Zinc's cash did not move at all while its three-month lost $43.00, taking its backwardation to $217.00. Selling concentrated in the back of the curve is what a macro trade looks like; it is not what a demand collapse looks like.

WHAT TO WATCH: whether aluminium's contango flips into backwardation, which at $3.50 is now one ordinary session away and would be the first genuine front-end tightness signal since mid-August; the 38.2% retracement at $3,254.60, now $38.60 overhead and the level that has capped this market since 18-August; and the Hormuz negotiating window, because on the evidence of the last three sessions single statements out of either capital are repricing this market in both directions faster than any fundamental is moving.

lme.commentary: THE 27-AUGUST SESSION IN ONE LINE: A UNIFORMLY RED BOARD WITH A UNIFORMLY TIGHTENING FRONT END. Aluminium cash settled $3,212.50, down $15.00 (-0.46%), and three-month $3,216.00, down $23.00 (-0.71%), giving back most of the previous session's $39.50 Hormuz-driven jump. Every metal here fell on the three-month and the EUR/USD LME fixing dropped to 1.16410 from 1.16690, so the first-order explanation is a firmer dollar rather than anything specific to aluminium. THE SECOND-ORDER READ IS THE INTERESTING ONE AND IT POINTS THE OTHER WAY. On every single metal the front outperformed the back. Aluminium's contango narrowed to $3.50 from $11.50 and $18.50 on 25-August - the flattest curve of the fifteen-session window and, at $3.50, within one ordinary session of flipping into backwardation. Copper's backwardation widened to $254.00 from $189.00, with cash off just $35.00 against a $100.00 fall in three-month and stock down 1,900 tonnes to 235,575, the lowest of the window. Zinc's cash did not move at all while its three-month lost $43.00, widening its backwardation to $217.00. Lead's contango narrowed to $31.00 on the only rising cash settlement on the board. When the whole complex sells the back of the curve and holds the front, that is a macro or currency trade being expressed in futures, not consumers walking away from metal. THE PHYSICAL LINE OFFERS NO OPINION EITHER WAY: exchange aluminium stock printed 246,825 tonnes for a third consecutive session with a published change of exactly zero. Three flat sessions is the absence of a signal. CONVENTION, RESTATED: cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO, the market declining to pay extra for prompt metal; cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION, the market paying up for it. Aluminium remains in contango for a ninth session - the front end is not yet tight - but the direction of travel this session was unambiguously toward tightness even as the headline price fell.

THE Q4-2026 ROUND HAS STILL NOT OPENED PUBLICLY: a dedicated search this run again returned no settlement, no offer range and no first-deal report, so Q4 is published on this board as a SCENARIO RANGE rather than as a number. Negotiations conventionally open in early September, now days away. THE BACKDROP THEY OPEN INTO CHANGED AGAIN OVERNIGHT AND IT CHANGED IN THE SELLERS' FAVOUR: the Iran-Oman corridor that looked like a de-escalation on 26-August was recast on 27-August by an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson who said the strait will not open unless the United States accepts Iran's conditions. Japanese buyers negotiating Q4 must now price a route that is still shut with no timetable, which is exactly the condition that produced the ten-year-high Q3 number. The scenario range on this board is widened at the top for that reason and the reason is stated rather than slipped in. NINETY-FIVE CENTS A POUND IS ABOUT $2,094/t. THE CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT THIS RUN IS THAT THE PREMISE OF THAT 8.2% SLUMP HAS NOT MATERIALISED AND HAS ARGUABLY GONE INTO REVERSE. On the public record: no proclamation reducing the Section 232 rate on Canadian aluminium has been published; US-Canada trade talks broke down; a separate 50% Section 338 tariff on a broad range of Canadian products took effect at 12:01 a.m. ET on Saturday 22-August after a three-day pause; and Canada issued retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on US imports as reported on 25-August. A premium that fell 8.2% on the expectation of tariff relief is sitting on an expectation that the subsequent week's events did not deliver. Against a duty-paid premium in the region of $2,094/t implied by the 20-August 95-cent Platts mark, the tariff leg is ROUGHLY 77% of the whole premium, up from about 76% yesterday. THE MECHANICAL POINT THAT MATTERS FOR ANYONE READING THIS ROW: because the tariff is ad valorem, a rally in the underlying metal automatically inflates the duty-paid premium even when nothing physical changes, and today is a clean example - the metal rose 1.24% and the tariff leg rose 1.24% with it. A premium that is more than three-quarters policy re-rates on a signature, and on this run the signature moved further away rather than closer: no Section 232 reduction proclamation has been published, US-Canada talks broke down, a 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian goods took effect 22-August and Canada retaliated. NO FREIGHT, FINANCING OR TIGHTNESS SPLIT IS PUBLISHED HERE BECAUSE NONE IS PUBLICLY SOURCED. drivers.text: THE TARIFF LEG OF THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN AND IT FELL TODAY - BECAUSE THE METAL PRICE FELL, NOT BECAUSE POLICY CHANGED — The Section 232 rate on aluminium ARTICLES is verified at 50% again this run and no reduction has been published. Applied to the 27-August cash official of $3,212.50 the arithmetic tariff component is 0.50 x $3,212.50 = $1,606.25 per tonne, DOWN from $1,613.75 yesterday purely because cash fell $15.00. Against the US Midwest duty-paid row at $2,094/t that leaves roughly $487.75 as the non-tariff, market-cleared remainder - the freight, financing, regional-tightness and margin content of the premium. THE DECOMPOSITION IS ARITHMETIC AND NOTHING MORE: it is tariff-rate times metal price against a published premium assessment. No split of the $487.75 remainder into freight versus financing versus tightness is offered anywhere on this page because no public source decomposes it, and inventing that breakdown would be fabrication. Note the structural consequence for a US buyer: because the tariff leg is a PERCENTAGE of the metal price, a falling LME automatically shrinks the duty burden in dollars per tonne, so US delivered cost falls faster than the LME does. Annex I-C carve-outs remain at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU, and the derivative-products rate remains 25%.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE OPERATIONAL FACT IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial shipping as at 27-August-2026. Around that fact the diplomacy has now reversed three times in three sessions and this row deliberately reports the reversals rather than smoothing them. On 25 and 26-August Iran and Oman outlined a PHASED FRAMEWORK for a temporary shipping corridor through the strait after weeks of negotiation, including a 30- to 60-day window to reach an understanding on a permanent and sustainable route, a joint initiative to clear mines from the waterway, and talks on the future administration of the strait; Oman's foreign minister said he was hopeful the two countries would soon formalise the arrangement. On 27-August a spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that the strait will not open under any circumstances unless the United States accepts Iran's conditions, and that statement has not been withdrawn. BOTH THINGS ARE PUBLICLY REPORTED AND THEY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The trend flag is therefore set to FLAT this run rather than up or down, because the evidence genuinely is two-sided and moving the flag daily on alternating statements would be noise. The test that would resolve it is not another announcement but a transit: no commercial vessel has yet moved under the framework. A public closure tracker showed the strait at day 179 at the time of this compile.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: CARRIED, WITH THE DIRECTION UNCHANGED AND REINFORCED BY THE HORMUZ NEWS. Suez transits have been recovering toward a two-year high as Red Sea routing risk normalises, which shortens Asia-Europe voyage distances and releases vessel capacity back into the global pool. If the Hormuz corridor plan holds, the two chokepoints normalise together and the freight-length premium built into Asia-Europe and Gulf-Asia aluminium and alumina routes compresses from both ends at once. That would be a genuine structural easing of delivered cost - and it is a conditional statement, not a forecast.

A reopened strait would remove war-risk surcharges and routing detours; it would NOT lower Capesize rates. A strait that stays shut does not raise them either. Freight is the stickier of the two costs inside every regional premium and it has been rising independently of the geopolitics. It is carried as the downstream half of the freight picture, and it is moving the same way as the dry-bulk half.

Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF EDGED UP TO EUR 68.66/MWh (+0.30%) ON 25-AUGUST - notably NOT following crude lower, which is the detail worth keeping. European gas is the marginal power input for the region's remaining primary capacity and the direct fuel input for alumina refining outside China, and it has its own supply geometry: LNG availability, storage trajectory into winter and Norwegian flows matter more to it than Gulf sentiment does. Two disruptions on this board run through gas rather than oil - the Alunorte refinery's gas-supply curtailment in Brazil and the Qatalum smelter's gas-driven shutdown - so gas is the energy price that has actually moved aluminium supply this year. A flat-to-firm TTF against falling crude says the energy complex is not de-escalating uniformly.

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: THE DOLLAR INDEX IS 98.95, ESSENTIALLY FLAT AT +0.04% ON THE TRADING ECONOMICS CROSS-ASSET BOARD AT THIS COMPILE. THAT MATTERS FOR HOW TODAY'S ALUMINIUM RALLY SHOULD BE READ, AND IT MATTERS IN THE CONSTRUCTIVE DIRECTION: a flat dollar means the 1.24% gain in cash and 1.01% in three-month is not a currency artefact. On 24 and 25-August this board attributed part of aluminium's underperformance to a firming dollar; that leg is absent today, so the move has to be explained by metal-specific and complex-specific factors - which on the evidence is the Hormuz reversal plus a broad base-metals bid that lifted four of five LME metals. Sub-99 on the DXY remains a historically undemanding level for dollar-denominated commodities. Source: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/aluminum

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD 1.1641 on the Trading Economics cross, corroborated by the 27-August LME FX fixing of 1.16410 (MTLE) against 1.16690 on 26-August and by the ECB fixing at 1.16450 against 1.16690. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL MACRO ROW ON THE BOARD TODAY. A dollar that firms roughly a quarter of a percent reprices every dollar-denominated metal lower without any metal-specific news, and that is exactly what the 27-August board shows: all five base metals down on the three-month with almost no dispersion between them. When the whole board moves together and nothing in the physical data moves at all - aluminium stock was unchanged for a third consecutive session - the currency is the explanation of first resort rather than of last resort. The cross-check that it is genuinely a dollar move and not a risk-off move: crude ROSE nearly 2% and European gas rose 4.4% on the same session, which is not the pattern of a general flight from risk assets.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: USD/CNY IS 6.7196 ON THE TRADING ECONOMICS BOARD AT THIS COMPILE, FLAT AT +0.03%. THE RELEVANCE FOR ALUMINIUM IS THE ARBITRAGE WINDOW BETWEEN SHANGHAI AND LONDON, AND TODAY THAT WINDOW MOVED AGAINST CHINESE EXPORTS: SHFE aluminium 2610 FELL 0.17% to 23,830 yuan/t on the same session the LME three-month official ROSE 1.01% to $3,239.00, with a flat currency in between. A widening London-over-Shanghai gap on an unchanged exchange rate improves the economics of moving Chinese metal out and, held long enough, is the mechanism by which Chinese surplus reaches the seaborne market. It is one session and no conclusion is drawn from it, but it is the opposite of the ratio repair this board reported earlier in the month. Source: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/aluminum

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR IS 4.646% ON THE TRADING ECONOMICS BOARD AT THIS COMPILE, UP a marginal 0.01%. A 4.6% handle on the long end is a real cost-of-carry number and it is the quiet argument against holding metal: financing inventory at these rates requires a contango wide enough to pay for it, and aluminium's $11.50 carry does not come close. THAT IS PART OF WHY THE LME WAREHOUSE LINE HAS GONE FLAT RATHER THAN REBUILDING - at 4.6% funding and an $11.50 three-month carry, warehousing aluminium is a losing trade before storage costs, so metal that leaves the exchange system is not being tempted back in. UK gilts at 4.98% and German bunds at 3.20% complete the picture of a global long end that remains restrictive for inventory financing everywhere, not just in dollars. Source: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/aluminum

headlines.title: THE ENTIRE BASE-METALS BOARD SETTLED LOWER ON 27-AUGUST AND THE CURRENCY IS THE SIMPLEST EXPLANATION. All five metals fell on the three-month - nickel -1.23%, zinc -1.09%, aluminium -0.71%, copper -0.70%, lead -0.21% - while the EUR/USD LME fixing fell to 1.16410 from 1.16690. A broad dollar move reprices a broad dollar-denominated board without any metal-specific news being required, and a uniformly red board with no dispersion is the signature of exactly that.

ALUMINIUM'S CONTANGO NARROWED TO $3.50 FROM $11.50 - THE FLATTEST CURVE OF THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW - BECAUSE CASH FELL $15.00 WHILE THREE-MONTH FELL $23.00. Spread and flat price moved in OPPOSITE directions. A ninth consecutive session in contango still means the front end is not tight, but at $3.50 the curve is effectively flat and one ordinary session from flipping into backwardation, which would be the first genuine prompt-tightness signal since mid-August.

EXCHANGE ALUMINIUM STOCK DID NOT MOVE FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION: 246,825 tonnes on 25, 26 and 27-August, with a published change of exactly zero each time. Three flat sessions is neither a draw nor a build - it is the complete absence of a physical signal, and it is the strongest evidence available that the last three sessions of price action have been driven by headlines and the dollar rather than by metal.

IRAN AND OMAN HAVE PUBLICLY OUTLINED A PHASED FRAMEWORK FOR A TEMPORARY SHIPPING CORRIDOR THROUGH THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ, with a 30- to 60-day window of continued negotiation aimed at a permanent and sustainable route, a joint initiative to clear mines from the waterway, and talks on the future administration of the strait. Oman's foreign minister said he was hopeful the two countries would soon formalise the arrangement. This is the de-escalation leg of a story that has now reversed twice in three sessions, and it is bearish for the risk premium - but only for the premium, because the strait itself remains effectively closed to commercial shipping and nothing has yet transited under the framework.

THE OPERATIONAL FACT HAS NOT CHANGED THROUGH ANY OF IT: THE STRAIT REMAINS EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO COMMERCIAL SHIPPING AS AT 27-AUGUST, and the 27-August Islamic Revolutionary Guard statement that the strait will not open unless the United States accepts Iran's conditions has not been withdrawn. A framework, a negotiating window and a hopeful foreign minister are not a transit. The asymmetry that has defined this market all month is intact: the premium prices out on announcements and back in on statements, while the physical route stays shut.

QATALUM IS REPORTED TO HAVE STABILISED AT ABOUT 60% OF NAMEPLATE - roughly 390,000 t/y or 32,500 t a month - having moved up from a full controlled shutdown, and EGA's Al Taweelah is running at about 18% of capacity with pre-war output guided to Q1-2027. Tomago in Australia has secured an A$2.5bn government support package to continue operating beyond 2028. Each of these is metal the market had already discounted returning on a dated, published schedule, and together they are the core of the bearish supply case that caps this recovery.

ALUNORTE - THE LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA - IS REPORTED OPERATING AT HALF CAPACITY ON A NATURAL-GAS SUPPLY FAILURE, and Hydro has publicly guided the Q3-2026 financial impact on its Bauxite and Alumina segment at USD 75-100 million. LNG supply from the Middle East, essential to refining, remains scarce under the tanker blockade. This is the single largest identified upward pressure on the alumina leg of the smelter cost curve and it is the main reason the alumina rows on this board are not read as benign despite an otherwise oversupplied market.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXPORTS ROSE 18.7% YEAR ON YEAR IN THE TWELVE MONTHS TO JULY. China has stepped up shipments as muted domestic demand allowed producers to export despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap, and those tonnes have been easing the shortage created by the Middle East disruption. The cap means Chinese primary output cannot grow indefinitely, but the export response shows the metal that does get produced is reaching the seaborne market rather than being absorbed at home.

LIZHONG GROUP REPORTED H1-2026 REVENUE OF RMB 18.822 BILLION, UP 30.32% YEAR ON YEAR, WITH NET PROFIT ATTRIBUTABLE OF RMB 577 MILLION, UP 43.81%. Its recycled aluminium alloy casting segment grew 35.16% to RMB 11.093 billion, aluminium alloy wheels 25.49% to RMB 6.236 billion and aluminium-based master alloys 17.87% to RMB 1.492 billion. Growth in production, sales and revenue across all three segments is a genuine downstream demand datapoint from a Chinese converter, and it sits awkwardly against the weak-demand narrative.

YINBANG CO. REPORTED H1-2026 REVENUE OF RMB 4.27 BILLION, UP 49.10% YEAR ON YEAR, AND NET PROFIT ATTRIBUTABLE OF RMB 88.538 MILLION, UP 95.08%, citing increased output of its main products and continued consolidation and expansion of market share. A second Chinese aluminium-processing name reporting both volume and margin expansion in the same week strengthens the read that converter-level demand is firmer than the ingot-inventory narrative alone would suggest.

YONGJIE NEW MATERIALS REPORTED H1-2026 REVENUE OF RMB 5.225 BILLION, UP 18.05%, AND NET PROFIT ATTRIBUTABLE OF RMB 514 MILLION, UP 176.65%. The company attributes the underlying improvement to product-mix optimisation and operating efficiency, and notes that the headline profit surge was amplified by the completion and consolidation of a major asset restructuring in the period - net profit excluding non-recurring items rose a more modest 31.12% to RMB 247 million. The ex-items figure is the one to read.

HINDALCO HAS COMMISSIONED INDIA'S FIRST SUPERFINE PRECIPITATED ALUMINIUM TRIHYDRATE (PPT ATH) PLANT AT BELAGAVI, KARNATAKA, with initial capacity of 30,000 tonnes a year and stated expandability to 60,000 tonnes, targeting halogen-free fire protection, wire and cable, polymer insulators, composites, paints and EV applications. This adds no primary smelting capacity - it is a specialty-alumina and downstream move - but it is further evidence of Indian producers investing through the cycle, and Indian volume growth remains one of the dated supply-relief items in the outlook.

COPPER'S BACKWARDATION WIDENED TO $254.00 FROM $189.00 WHILE ITS FLAT PRICE FELL 0.70%, on stock down another 1,900 tonnes to 235,575 - the lowest of the fifteen-session window. Zinc's cash did not move at all while its three-month lost $43.00, taking its backwardation to $217.00, the widest in percentage terms on the board, even as zinc stock ROSE 550 tonnes to 97,875. Across the whole board on 27-August the front end outperformed the back, which is the signature of macro selling rather than of demand failure.

NO SECTION 232 REDUCTION HAS BEEN PUBLISHED AND THE RATE ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES REMAINS 50%, while a SEPARATE 50% SECTION 338 DUTY ON CANADIAN GOODS took effect on 22-August. Canada is the largest external supplier of primary aluminium into the United States, so the structural input into the US duty-paid premium has moved against importers rather than for them. Priced-in relief that has no published legal basis is itself a premium risk.

THE JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLED AT $395/t CIF JAPAN FOR Q3-2026, up from $351.50 in Q2, $195.00 in Q1 and $86.00 in Q4-2025 - a near five-fold rise across four quarters and the clearest single quantification of what the Middle East disruption has done to Asian delivered cost. The Q4-2026 round has not opened publicly and is carried on this board as a $310-400 scenario range with a null value, held unchanged this run rather than churned on alternating daily Hormuz statements.

KIRIN IS EXPLORING GREATER USE OF RECYCLED AND LOW-CARBON ALUMINIUM IN PACKAGING, including GHG-free metal produced with renewable energy and high-recycled-content material, and estimates carbon pricing could add JPY 43.8 billion (USD 275.4 million) to its packaging costs by 2050 under a stronger low-carbon transition scenario. It expects to spend about JPY 200 million between 2025 and 2027 on recycled and green aluminium and low-carbon malt, rising to JPY 4.7 billion by 2030. Read as a demand-mix signal: the tonnes stay, but the premium migrates toward certified low-carbon and recycled units.

BRENT ROSE 1.98% TO $89.58 AND WTI 1.59% TO $83.54 ON THE SAME SESSION THAT THE WHOLE METALS BOARD FELL, while European TTF gas rose 4.38% to EUR 68.66/MWh. Firmer energy raises the marginal smelter's power and the refinery's gas cost - a cost-push support for the metal - at the same time as a firmer dollar pushed the metal price down. The two forces are pulling in opposite directions and the currency won the session.

A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

trade.note: TRADE-CORRIDOR MAP REVIEWED ON A MATERIAL-CHANGE TRIGGER THIS RUN RATHER THAN ON THE MONTHLY CYCLE, BECAUSE THE 26-AUGUST HORMUZ ANNOUNCEMENT IS EXACTLY THE KIND OF EVENT THE TRIGGER EXISTS FOR - and the conclusion is that the corridor entries are NOT changed yet, deliberately. Iran and Oman announced a plan for a mutually agreed safe maritime corridor roughly seven nautical miles wide, described as TEMPORARY with a permanent route to be negotiated in 30 to 60 days; a US-Iran ceasefire including freedom of navigation is reported but UNCONFIRMED by either government; and Iran's deputy foreign minister stated EXPLICITLY that the memorandum does not mean the strait reopens on 26-August. A corridor that is planned, temporary and not yet operating is not a restored trade route, and re-drawing the flow map on an announcement rather than on transits would be exactly the kind of premature reclassification this map is designed to avoid. THE TRIGGER FOR CHANGING THESE ENTRIES IS STATED SO IT CAN BE HELD TO: confirmed resumption of commercial transits, or a permanent-route agreement, whichever comes first. The second live trigger on this map is unrelated and is a US proclamation altering the Canadian tariff rate, which would change the North American corridor economics rather than the Gulf ones. REVIEW NOTE, 27-AUGUST: the corridor map is reviewed monthly or on material change and is NOT churned daily. It was reviewed on this run and the flows are held unchanged, because nothing physical changed - the Strait of Hormuz has been shut throughout and remains shut. What changed is rhetoric in both directions inside three sessions: an Iran-Oman safe-corridor plan announced 26-August, then an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps statement on 27-August that the strait will not open under any circumstances unless the United States accepts Iran's conditions. A corridor map is redrawn when ships move, not when statements are issued. The one trade-policy change since the last review that IS reflected in the commentary elsewhere on this board is the US-Canada escalation: a 50% Section 338 tariff on a broad range of Canadian products effective 22-August and Canadian retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% reported 25-August.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.
src: AL Circle - China eases aluminium shortage after Iran war, but pressure shifts to Western fabricators, 18-Aug-2026

flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June, and on the published aggregate the IAI's June-2026 release (20-July-2026) showed global primary output down 1.5% y/y; a widely repeated 'outside-China -6.7% y/y in July' figure could not be traced to a dated IAI release at this refresh and is not carried here. Transit has been the binding constraint rather than production - but production is also impaired in its own right: EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots on 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar and confirmed still shut in its 04-Aug Q2 disclosure. THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.
src: Bloomberg / Kpler via public reporting - Iran-Oman Hormuz route agreement and transit counts (05-Aug-2026)

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. Bab al Mandeb traffic fell to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared 20-Jul and claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. On 05-Aug Houthi forces claimed they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

~60% of global primary output; the 45 Mt capacity cap is binding at 45.31 Mt/y operating. The July twist is compositional: the liquid-aluminium proportion rose to 78.3% with casting-ingot volume -15.1% y/y, so less deliverable ingot reaches the domestic market even at capped output - semis exports remain the swing valve between the domestic balance and the ex-China deficit.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LONDON RING PRINTS THE 28-AUGUST OFFICIAL SETTLEMENT AND THE SPECIFIC THING TO WATCH IS THE SPREAD, NOT THE PRICE. The curve closed 27-August at a $3.50 contango, the flattest of the fifteen-session window, having narrowed from $11.50 and $18.50 in two sessions. One ordinary session's move flips it into backwardation, which would be the first genuine prompt-tightness signal since mid-August and would matter considerably more than another $20 on the flat price. Watch also whether the exchange stock line moves at all after three consecutive sessions unchanged at 246,825 tonnes.

THE IRAN-OMAN CORRIDOR FRAMEWORK EITHER PRODUCES A TRANSIT OR IT PRODUCES ANOTHER STATEMENT. The framework carries a 30- to 60-day negotiating window toward a permanent route and a joint mine-clearing initiative, and Oman's foreign minister has said he is hopeful of early formalisation - but the strait remains effectively closed and the 27-August Islamic Revolutionary Guard statement that it will not open without US terms stands. The market has repriced this in both directions on three consecutive sessions. The distinguishing test is a vessel actually moving, because every announcement so far has been made with the route shut.

THE SEPTEMBER-OCTOBER CHINESE PEAK SEASON IS THE NEXT REAL DEMAND TEST AND THE EVIDENCE INTO IT HAS JUST IMPROVED. Three Chinese converters reported H1-2026 growth on 28-August - Lizhong +30.32% revenue, Yinbang +49.10%, Yongjie +18.05% - which is a firmer starting point than the ingot-inventory narrative alone implies. What would confirm it is a resumption of the exchange stock draw, which has now stalled completely for three sessions, and a sustained pickup in downstream operating rates.

CHINESE SOCIAL INVENTORY AND DOWNSTREAM OPERATING-RATE PRINTS PUBLISH WEEKLY AND ARE THE HIGHEST-FREQUENCY PHYSICAL SERIES AVAILABLE ON THIS MARKET. No newer public SMM aluminium morning-meeting edition than 27-August was retrievable at this compile, so no Chinese inventory figure has been refreshed on this run and none is presented as a 28-August print. The next edition is the item to check first.

THE JAPANESE Q4-2026 QUARTERLY PREMIUM NEGOTIATION HAS NOT OPENED PUBLICLY. Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan, up from $351.50 in Q2, $195.00 in Q1 and $86.00 in Q4-2025. This board carries Q4 as a $310-400 scenario range with a NULL value and will continue to do so until a public settlement prints. The range was held unchanged this run rather than moved on alternating daily Hormuz statements.

EGA'S AL TAWEELAH IS GUIDED TO RETURN TO PRE-WAR OUTPUT LEVELS IN Q1-2027 FROM ABOUT 18% OF CAPACITY TODAY, and Qatalum is reported already stabilised near 60% of nameplate having restarted from a full shutdown. Together with Tomago underwritten beyond 2028 by an A$2.5bn Australian support package, this is the dated, published supply-relief schedule that caps the medium-term recovery. It is the single most important bearish structural item on this board and none of it depends on a forecast.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD AND TODAY'S RALLY DOES NOTHING TO IT. SMM's 27-August morning meeting repeats the aggregate verbatim: outside China, driven by new capacity and production resumptions, daily average production is expected to CONTINUE rebounding. The asset-level schedule beneath that sentence is EGA restoring Al Taweelah from ~18% of capacity toward pre-war output in Q1-2027, Century Aluminum holding 2026 guidance at 630 kt while ramping idled capacity, and Alcoa's Portland and San Ciprian restarts already complete. A NEW STRUCTURAL ITEM IS ADDED THIS RUN: the Alcoa-South32 binding conditional agreement of 01-July concentrates non-Chinese smelting and alumina capacity - including the Hillside smelter - in a single owner with a demonstrated restart record, which removes no tonnes and plausibly runs assets harder. This is not a forecast of supply; it is a published timetable of it.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED AND NINE SESSIONS NOW CONFIRM IT - AND TODAY IS THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE YET BECAUSE THE PRICE ROSE 1.24% WHILE THE WAREHOUSE LINE MOVED EXACTLY ZERO TONNES. LME aluminium stock went from 303,675 tonnes at end-June to 246,925 by 17-August, a 56,750-tonne draw, and has since moved a NET 100 TONNES to 246,825. That is 0.04% of the total and roughly forty minutes of global output. A rally with no draw and an eighth consecutive session of contango is a sentiment rally, and the correct inference is that the tightness argument at the LME front end is not currently supported by the inventory data. The offsetting Chinese draw is real - 23,000 tonnes week on week to 852,000 tonnes - but it is a Chinese phenomenon and it has not transmitted to the exchange.

TREND MOVED TO FLAT THIS RUN, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The Hormuz premium has now repriced in BOTH directions across three consecutive sessions - out on the 25/26-August Iran-Oman phased-framework announcement, back in on the 27-August Islamic Revolutionary Guard statement that the strait will not open without US terms, and partly out again on 27-August as the framework detail (a 30-to-60-day negotiating window toward a permanent route, plus a joint mine-clearing initiative, with Oman's foreign minister hopeful of early formalisation) was reported more fully. Setting this flag up or down on alternating daily statements would be noise dressed as analysis, so it is set FLAT: the two-sided evidence is the honest description of the current state. THE UNDERLYING OPERATIONAL FACT HAS NOT CHANGED THROUGH ANY OF IT - the strait remains effectively closed to commercial shipping and no vessel has transited under the framework. The asymmetry to keep in mind is that the premium is currently priced closer to the de-escalation case than to the closure case, so a breakdown in the talks would reprice it UP violently, while an actual first transit would take further premium out in an orderly way. THE HORMUZ RISK PREMIUM IS NOW REPRICING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON STATEMENTS RATHER THAN ON SHIPPING - TREND MOVED BACK FROM DOWN TO UP THIS RUN, ONE SESSION AFTER BEING MOVED DOWN, AND THE REVERSAL IS DELIBERATE AND STATED. On 26-August Iran and Oman announced a plan for a temporary ~7-nautical-mile safe corridor and this board moved the flag DOWN for the first time since the closure began, while warning explicitly that a breakdown would reprice the premium back UP violently. On 27-August an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson said the strait belongs to Iran and Oman, that agreement on waters and revenue shares was already reached, that the United States obstructed it, and that the strait will NOT be open under any circumstances unless the United States accepts Iran's conditions; the US President said he has no timetable and is not in a hurry. THE OPERATIONAL FACT NEVER CHANGED: THE STRAIT HAS BEEN SHUT THROUGHOUT. The risk is that a market repricing a closed waterway twice in three sessions on rhetoric will do it again, and position sizing against a headline nobody can forecast is the real exposure here.

TREND MOVED FROM UP TO DOWN THIS RUN ON NEW PUBLIC EVIDENCE, AND THE EVIDENCE IS CONVERTER EARNINGS RATHER THAN SENTIMENT. Three Chinese aluminium processors reported H1-2026 results on 28-August and all three grew: Lizhong Group revenue RMB 18.822bn (+30.32%) with net profit RMB 577m (+43.81%) and growth in production, sales and revenue across all three of its segments; Yinbang Co. revenue RMB 4.27bn (+49.10%) with net profit RMB 88.538m (+95.08%) on increased output of main products; Yongjie New Materials revenue RMB 5.225bn (+18.05%) with net profit ex-non-recurring items RMB 247m (+31.12%). These are audited half-year converter numbers, not survey sentiment, and they are hard to reconcile with a thesis that physical demand is failing. The risk is not eliminated - half-year results are backward-looking and say nothing about September-October - but the direction of the evidence moved against the risk this run. PHYSICAL DEMAND FAILS TO SHOW UP FOR THE PEAK SEASON, AND THE ALLOY CHAIN IS NOW THE CLEAREST EVIDENCE. SMM's 27-August meeting states that although the traditional peak season is about to arrive, expectations of peak-season stockpiling have YET TO MATERIALISE and the market holds a wait-and-see attitude. The corroboration is specific and it got stronger this run: China's social inventory of cast aluminium alloy ingots rose 3,700 tonnes week on week to 31,800 tonnes, a THIRD consecutive week of buildup, with die-casters buying just-in-time; SMM expects the buildup to continue. Central China spot transacted at a DISCOUNT of 80-120 yuan/t to the SHFE September contract as buyers refused to chase the rally. Primary ingot drawing while alloy builds and downstream refuses higher prices is a market where the draw is not consumption-led.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. Trend held at DOWN, and today's session marginally reduces the residual risk rather than raising it: a 1.24% cash gain with the front end leading and the contango narrowing is not the signature of forced liquidation. The honest qualification is that no public positioning data was retrievable this run and the read is inferential. What is observable is that the market has now had a two-day sell-off and a one-day recovery inside a $56 range off the 20-August low without breaking it, which is consistent with a position base that has already been substantially cleared rather than one still to be cleared.

TREND MOVED FROM DOWN TO UP THIS RUN. Alunorte, the largest alumina refinery outside China, is reported operating at roughly half capacity on a natural-gas supply failure, and Hydro has publicly guided the Q3-2026 impact on its Bauxite and Alumina segment at USD 75-100 million. Middle East LNG, essential to refining, remains scarce under the tanker blockade. A named refinery of that scale running at half rates with a quantified earnings impact is materially more concrete evidence of an alumina cost shock than this row carried last run. AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. Trend held at DOWN. No newer public alumina assessment than the marks already carried on this board was retrievable this run and nothing has been moved: FOB East Australia is held at $356/t at its 05-August SMM-reported transaction date, and the China spot and capacity-utilisation picture is carried at its own dates. The reason the trend stays DOWN rather than being lifted is that the last cleanly dated Chinese evidence pointed lower - spot expected at 2,550-2,650 yuan/t and grinding down, national capacity utilisation rising, trader inventories building - and nothing published since contradicts it. The residual risk is seaborne rather than Chinese, and it is genuinely two-sided while Gulf logistics remain unresolved.

TREND MOVED FROM DOWN TO UP THIS RUN AND THE REVERSAL IS EXPLICIT. Last run this row was flagged DOWN on a 3.16% fall in Brent. On 27-August that reversed: Brent rose 1.98% to $89.58, WTI rose 1.59% to $83.54 and European TTF gas rose 4.38% to EUR 68.66/MWh in a single session. Gas is the direct input to alumina refining and a large input to European smelter power, so a 4.4% one-session move in TTF is the more important of the two. SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE. TREND HELD AT DOWN AND THE EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED SHARPLY THIS RUN. Brent fell 3.16% to $85.78 and WTI 3.06% to $79.84 on the Trading Economics board at this compile, following declines of 2.57% on 24-August and 1.16% on 25-August; Brent has now given back the whole of the two-week advance that carried it above $94. European gas fell 3.68% to EUR 64.27, so the energy complex IS easing broadly this run rather than divergently as it was yesterday. Petroleum coke is a refinery co-product loosely tethered to the crude complex, so this is disinflationary for the carbon leg with a lag. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS UNCHANGED AND IT MATTERS: it has NOT yet appeared in any published coke, pitch or anode mark - no CPC, green coke, CTP or prebaked anode figure newer than mid-August was publicly retrievable - and coal tar pitch at its 13-August mark of ~4,960 yuan/t is still up from 4,705 on 23-July.

US TRADE POLICY MOVES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM - AND THE RISK IS NOW THAT PRICED-IN RELIEF DOES NOT ARRIVE, WHICH IS A REVERSAL OF HOW THIS ROW READ LAST WEEK. The September US Midwest premium slumped 8.2% to 95 cents a pound on 20-August and October-November contracts fell more than 12%, on reports the United States was set to cut Section 232 tariffs on Canadian metal to 25% from 50%. Since then, on the public record: NO proclamation has been published; US-Canada talks broke down; a separate 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian goods took effect 22-August after a three-day pause; and Canada issued retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% as reported 25-August. At the unchanged 50% rate on today's $3,227.50 cash the tariff leg is $1,613.75/t of a roughly $2,094/t duty-paid premium - about 77%, and it rose $19.75 today purely because the metal rose. A premium that is three-quarters policy re-rates on a signature, and the signature has moved further away.

FREIGHT AND DELIVERED-COST INFLATION INSIDE EVERY REGIONAL PREMIUM. The Baltic Dry stands at 2,882 on its 24-August print, up 1.44% and a third consecutive gain, Capesize-led at 4,643 (+2.0%); no 25, 26 or 27-August print was publicly retrievable at this compile and the row is held at its date. Guinea-to-China freight at roughly $35-38/t against delivered ore of $70-74/t means ocean freight is approaching half the delivered cost of the ore. THE POINT THAT MATTERS AGAINST A HORMUZ NARRATIVE THAT HAS NOW FLIPPED TWICE IN THREE SESSIONS: dry bulk freight is set by vessel supply and bulk demand, not by one waterway. Neither a reopening nor a continued closure moves Capesize rates. Freight is the stickier of the two costs inside every regional premium and it is still rising.

CARBON BORDER POLICY AND CERTIFICATION BECOME CONDITIONS OF MARKET ACCESS RATHER THAN DIFFERENTIATORS. Hindalco's Baphlimali mine became India's first ASI-certified bauxite operation under Performance Standard V3.1, extending a certified chain into roughly 2.67 Mt/yr of alumina and taking the group to eleven certified sites. Read alongside the EU's carbon border mechanism and the growing low-carbon premium channels, certification is migrating from a marketing claim to an entry requirement for the highest-value European and downstream channels. A related structural item this run: SMM reports the EU's tariff increase and the UAE's scrap export ban are contracting European and Middle Eastern scrap supply, with China's July scrap imports down to ~119,600 tonnes from 133,000 in June - trade policy is reshaping the recycled leg of the chain as well as the primary one. This is a slow risk with a long fuse and it is carried for that reason.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

The premium has repriced in BOTH directions across three consecutive sessions: out on the 25/26-August Iran-Oman phased-framework announcement, back in on the 27-August Islamic Revolutionary Guard statement that the strait will not open without US terms, and partly out again as the framework detail was reported more fully. Both sets of statements are publicly reported and neither has been withdrawn. The underlying operational fact never changed: the strait remains effectively closed to commercial shipping and no vessel has transited under the framework.

THE CROSS-ASSET DIVERGENCE BETWEEN CRUDE AND ALUMINIUM HAS NOW REVERSED SIGN IN ONE SESSION AND IS FLAGGED AS UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN EXPLAINED. On 26-August Brent fell 3.16% while aluminium rose 1.24%; on 27-August Brent rose 1.98% while aluminium fell 0.71%. Two consecutive sessions of opposite-direction moves is not a stable relationship and no causal story is constructed from it on this board. What is stated without inference: firmer crude and materially firmer European gas raise smelter power and alumina refining costs, which is cost-push support beneath the metal regardless of the day's price direction.

THE JULY AVERAGE COLUMNS ARE CARRIED UNCHANGED BECAUSE THE MONTH HAS NOT ROLLED. Every 'average' column on the LME benchmark table and the LME Board detail rows is the PRIOR-MONTH (July-2026) mean and will not change until 1-September. The August month-to-date cash averages computed across all nineteen published August sessions are stated separately in the base-metals series basis note and are the figures used to update the rebased history series.

ALUMINA, BAUXITE, CAUSTIC, LIME AND EVERY INPUT-BASKET ROW OTHER THAN COPPER ARE CARRIED AT THEIR OWN DATED PUBLIC MARKS BECAUSE NO NEWER PUBLIC EDITION WAS RETRIEVABLE THIS RUN. Rows with no public series at all - smelter electricity, cathode and graphite blocks, and Ti-B grain refiner - carry EMPTY trend histories by design, and their source notes state why. Nothing on this board is interpolated or estimated to fill a gap: sparse two-and-three-point series on periodic settlement cycles are correct, not incomplete.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC MARKET INFORMATION FROM CITED PUBLIC SOURCES. This dashboard contains no confidential, internal or company-specific data of any kind - no realised prices, no net-backs, no shipping lanes, no volumes, no costs and no internal commentary - and it is not framed as any particular company's tool or position. The only company-specific content is public listed-company information in the peer-earnings and producer-status panels, all of it sourced to public disclosures or press.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE SECTION IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, AND ITS INVALIDATION LEVELS ARE STATED IN PRICE SO THE COUNT CAN BE FALSIFIED: 3,159.50 on the daily degree and a weekly close below 3,061.50 on the position degree. Confidence is stated as MODERATE on both degrees, and deliberately not higher, because the recent range has been set by geopolitical statements and by the dollar rather than by structure.
